title: an ambient Error declaration introduces no runtime binding, so nothing may be emitted that names it
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Error Classes': "The compiler MUST provide stable nominal identity, matching metadata, serialization evidence, and cross-realm transport metadata while preserving ordinary `Error` behavior." The obligation is about classes the compiler emits; `declare class` emits nothing, and the last clause — preserving ordinary behavior — is violated outright by a program that cannot load. WHAT THIS PINS is the registration SITE, not the identity: an ambient Error class still RESERVES its name, and only the emitted `__vsRegisterError(...)` call is withheld. Both halves were measured rather than assumed. Before the fix the reference compiled this file with zero diagnostics and the emitted module died while it was still loading — `ReferenceError: Ambient is not defined` at `__vsRegisterError(Ambient, "smithers:an-ambient-error-declaration-is-not-registered.sm:Ambient")`, exit 1 — which is the failure mode this case is filed against: a clean compile that cannot run. The fix is one predicate, `emitsNoRuntimeBinding` in poc/src/language/compile.ts, asked once at the class-declaration lowering site; `collectErrorDeclarations` is untouched, so the SMITHERS1150 duplicate-name refusal is unchanged. THE RESERVATION HALF WAS MEASURED SEPARATELY, because a guard placed one level too early would have silently deleted it and this case could not have noticed: two same-named ambient Error classes in one file still report `SMITHERS1150@5:15` on BOTH backends after the fix. The predicate reads `ts.NodeFlags.Ambient`, the binder's own answer, which covers a `declare` modifier on the declaration and an enclosing ambient container alike, where `getCombinedModifierFlags` would see only the first. The Go fork draws the line in the same place — `isNominalErrorClass` unchanged, an ambient guard at its registration site — so the two backends now agree here instead of deliberately differing.
